paragraphs.text: **A revenue line, not a fund.** The tuition is counted as revenue of the Town’s general fund. Nothing is spent from the line, and it does not carry over: each year it starts again at zero.
**Not a revolving fund.** In a revolving fund, such as Extended Day, the fees stay with the program and pay its costs. The school’s books credit none of this tuition to the preschool.

**Above plan, it becomes part of free cash.** The $53,657 received above what the Town planned on in FY2025 is part of the receipts over estimate that the state counts when it certifies free cash. That is how Massachusetts free cash is calculated; we have not seen the Town’s own closing entry for this account.

blocks.title: What kind of account this is

paragraphs.text: **The school budget names no preschool line.** No account, organization or budget line is named for it, and the account codes put the preschool in with the whole Primary School. A “P.S.” in a line name is the Primary School, never the preschool.
**Only the IDEA preschool grants are identifiable**: DESE codes 262, 264 and 298, each on its own fund page.

**Staff pay is our match**: the annual report’s Primary School roster lists teachers and paraprofessionals under a preschool heading, and its wage list prints each name’s gross pay. We matched the two and publish only the total. A year is shown only when every post matched.
**The preschool is integrated**: children on education plans and tuition-paying children share it, so even a full staff cost would not separate the two.

The School Committee votes the rate each year. On 7 February 2024 it raised the FY2025 rate by 4%: two days a week to $1,897.11, four days to $3,548.58. It approved 4% again for FY2026 on 22 January 2025, and for FY2027 on 21 January 2026, adding a five-day option.
